title: The Primary and Secondary Corporate Credit Facilities

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: This Federal Reserve Bank of New York staff report provides a comprehensive overview of the Primary Market Corporate Credit Facility (PMCCF) and Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facility (SMCCF), designed to restore functioning in corporate bond markets during the COVID-19 pandemic. The report documents that yield spreads widened approximately 250 bps for investment-grade bonds and 550 bps for high-yield bonds in March 2020, with nearly $200 billion in outflows from corporate bond funds. The SMCCF made total purchases of $14 billion before ceasing operations on December 31, 2020.
key_points: The SMCCF commenced ETF purchases on May 12, 2020 and bond purchases on June 16, 2020, making total purchases of $14 billion
The PMCCF became operational on June 29, 2020, but no qualified borrower ever expressed the need to use the facility
In the last two weeks of March 2020, mutual funds and ETFs specializing in corporate bonds experienced nearly $200 billion in outflows
Yield spreads widened approximately 250 bps for investment-grade bonds and 550 bps for high-yield bonds during the March 2020 dislocation
High-yield corporate bond issuance halted entirely between March 4 and April 16, 2020
The CCFs were authorized under Section 13(3) of the Federal Reserve Act and supported by the U.S. Treasury
Bid-ask spreads in corporate bonds deteriorated to levels not seen since the Global Financial Crisis
The SMCCF portfolio wind-down was announced June 2, 2021 and completed by August 31, 2021
why_it_matters: This research paper documents a significant Federal Reserve intervention in corporate credit markets and provides empirical evidence on how emergency lending facilities can restore market functioning. The findings on how official sector backstops reassured issuers and investors are relevant for understanding future market stress scenarios and the design of similar facilities.
macro_context: The CCFs were designed to facilitate credit provision to the non-financial corporate sector during the COVID-19 pandemic. By providing a backstop to investment-grade corporate debt issuers, the facilities aimed to enable companies to continue employing workers and funding working capital during pandemic-related shutdowns.
market_structure_context: The paper details how corporate bond market liquidity deteriorated dramatically during March 2020, with bid-ask spreads reaching GFC-levels. The SMCCF purchased both corporate bonds and ETFs (through iShares iBoxx $ Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF and Invesco Senior Loan ETF) to restore market functioning.
